description.value: Lakeshore Campground is the Columbia Valley's largest lakefront campground and the only one situated directly on the shores of Lake Windermere, operated by the ʔakisq̓nuk First Nation on Ktunaxa territory with over 10,000 years of Indigenous history. It offers 14 serviced lots with 30-amp electrical, 51 non-serviced lots, and 62 seasonal sites, with mountain views, lake access, showers, walking trails, and a playground. Touring cyclists will find nearby trail networks (Mount Swansea, Old Coach Trail, Westside Legacy Trail) just minutes away, plus easy access to Radium Hot Springs and Invermere.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Primary evidence is the website content fetched from lakeshorecampground.ca. The site confirms address (3151 Hwy 93/95, Windermere, BC V0A 2L2), phone (250-342-6352), and open status (May–October). The Stay Here page explicitly lists showers, 30-amp electrical serviced lots, and a Book Now booking system; it also mentions a convenience store and food options 7 minutes away in Windermere. The OSM name includes '& Campground' while the website consistently uses 'Lakeshore Campground,' though the Stay Here page does refer to it as 'Lakeshore Resort' — flagged as a minor discrepancy.
concerns: OSM name is 'Lakeshore Resort & Campground' but the website domain and most page titles use 'Lakeshore Campground'; the Stay Here page does refer to it as 'Lakeshore Resort,' suggesting the OSM name may be a combined form not used as a single official name.
OSM record has no osm_id or matched tags — this appears to be a manually added candidate rather than a verified OSM node.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, operating, publicly accessible campground on Lake Windermere with confirmed contact details, active booking system, and clear relevance to touring cyclists.
enrichment_extras.notes: Campground is Indigenous-owned and operated by the ʔakisq̓nuk First Nation on Ktunaxa territory — a notable cultural distinction worth highlighting in the directory.
